headline: No shared channels or write surfaces are exposed; the main residual risk is low-probability prompt/cascade misuse from document outputs into data-engineering workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker exposes no filesystem read/write, shell, browser, subprocess, or MCP surfaces, and RisingWave exposes no shared channel or ingestion path in the profile. With no documented bridge, a prompt-injection pathway between them is not plausible from the available profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through copy-paste, shared files, or MCP, reassess injection risk.
IF a hidden orchestration layer forwards outputs between them, the pathway may exist.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared clipboard or file handoff.
Disable any future MCP or queue bridge unless provenance is tracked.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows data classes touched, filesystem access, or network egress; Marker cannot read files and RisingWave has no documented input surface here. The pair therefore lacks a documented route for sensitive data to flow from one agent to the other.
conditions: IF either agent is given shared workspace access, leakage risk changes.
IF future configuration adds file ingestion or export, reassess data exposure.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Document data classes before enabling new inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker has no write, shell, or git modification capability, and RisingWave is marked runnable false with no write surface exposed. Without overlapping mutable-resource access, there is no credible capability conflict in the current profiles.
conditions: IF RisingWave is deployed with write access to the same resources as Marker, conflict risk may appear.
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents mutable shared state, reassess.
mitigations: Do not grant git or filesystem write permissions to Marker.
Verify RisingWave remains non-runnable in this pairing.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker is a document-processing agent, so its outputs could be consumed by RisingWave in a downstream pipeline, but the profiles do not show an automatic handoff or action-taking authority. Any cascade would require an added integration, so the blast radius is limited and not default.
conditions: IF RisingWave is configured to treat Marker output as authoritative input, cascade risk increases.
IF Marker output is used to drive automated ETL or database actions, reassess severity.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream use.
Validate Marker outputs against schema or tests.
Log and diff transformed records before commit.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent, and neither profile lists sensitive data classes. With only docs-level information, there is no compliance violation pathway to attribute to this pair.
conditions: IF either vendor later documents conflicting residency or retention terms, reassess.
IF PHI, EU PII, or regulated data is introduced, compliance analysis changes.
mitigations: Record residency and retention terms before use.
Avoid regulated data until policies are confirmed.
